policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV reads a plural verb, "And they commanded the children of Benjamin", matching the qere plural wayyetsawwu; the defectively written ketiv ויצו is the singular wayyetsaw, "and he commanded", which the ASV does not render.

ASV "come to complain unto us" renders la-rib, the infinitive of rib "to contend/complain"; the ketiv לרוב belongs to a different root and yields no sense of complaint. The two notes here are classed alternative_rendering ("Or, strive with us" is another English word for the same rib, "Or, as a gift" touches a different clause) and so neither decides the unit, but the main text's wording does.
